title: Revising Context, Shifting Simulated Stance: Auditing LLM-Based Stance Simulation in Online Discussions
abstract: arXiv:2606.06443v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate social media users and infer how individuals may respond to online discussions. However, it remains unclear whether these simulations reflect precise user-specific beliefs or whether they are highly sensitive to semantically independent changes in conversational contexts. In this work, we study counterfactual context revision as a framework for auditing LLM-based stance simulation. Given an original online conversation, we first infer a target user's stance toward a specific topic. translated_title: 修改语境，转变模拟立场：审计基于大语言模型的在线讨论立场模拟
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于模拟社交媒体用户，并推断个体可能如何回应在线讨论。然而，这些模拟究竟反映了用户特定的精确信念，还是对语义上独立的对话语境变化高度敏感，目前仍不清楚。在本工作中，我们研究反事实语境修改，将其作为审计基于大语言模型的立场模拟的框架。给定一段原始在线对话，我们首先推断目标用户对特定话题的立场，然后对对话语境应用受控的修改策略，并在修改后的语境下再次模拟用户的立场。我们将纯文本修改策略与融合表情包语境的多模态修改策略进行比较，并评估两个主要的有效性指标，即平均方向性立场偏移和立场转变率。结果显示了有效且稳健的立场转变。
tldr: 本文提出以反事实语境修改为框架来审计大语言模型的立场模拟，通过对在线对话语境进行受控修改（包括纯文本与表情包多模态策略）并测量立场偏移与转变率，揭示了LLM模拟立场对语境变化的高度敏感性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes counterfactual context revision as a framework for auditing LLM-based stance simulation, applying controlled context revisions (text-only and multimodal meme-based) to online discussions and measuring stance shift and transition rates to reveal the sensitivity of simulated stances to context changes.
